passage:
Subject: The vendor review

Hi Amandeep,

I know you wanted the team-lead role, and I know it is awkward that I got it. Over the last two weeks I've felt the coolness, and it stung, but I'm not asking you to be warm on demand.

I do want to say that your handling of the supplier disputes last year was the best on the team. I'd like you to lead the vendor review this quarter, with full say on the plan. My job is to clear blocks, not to hover.

If you'd like to tell me how you feel about all this, my door is open. If not, that's fine too.

Chandrika

qa.q: What does Chandrika ask Amandeep to lead this quarter?
qa.a: Chandrika asks Amandeep to lead the vendor review, with full say on the plan.

qa.q: How does Chandrika feel about the cool treatment?
qa.a: Hurt: the coolness stung, but Chandrika isn't demanding warmth.

qa.q: How does Chandrika respond to the envy?
qa.a: By acknowledging Amandeep's strengths, giving meaningful work and letting time settle things rather than demanding warmth.

qa.q: How might Amandeep be feeling about the promotion?
qa.a: Disappointed, since Amandeep wanted the role, and perhaps unsure whether the offer of the review is genuine.

grounding: Former peers who wanted the promotion are cool toward Chandrika, who stays generous, acknowledges strengths and gives meaningful work.

passage:
The app launch was in three days, the office AC had broken, and Ritu had been team lead for exactly two weeks. At the morning stand-up, Vishal, who had also applied for the job, said, "Whatever the boss decides," with a little bow. Two people laughed.

Ritu felt the sting right in her chest. She wanted to snap back. She had a launch to run.

She waited until lunch. Vishal was the best tester on the team; everyone knew it. She found him at his desk. "I need someone to own the final testing plan. You catch things nobody else does. Will you lead it?"

He looked up, suspicious. "Why me?"

"Because you're the best at it."

He shrugged. "Fine."

He was still cool that week, and he still made one sarcastic joke. Ritu let it go. But on launch night, he stayed till two, found three critical bugs, and at the end said, "Good launch," without a bow.

qa.q: How many critical bugs did Vishal find on launch night?
What did Ritu feel when Vishal bowed at the stand-up?
qa.a: Ritu felt hurt, a sting in her chest, and tempted to snap back.

qa.q: How did Ritu respond to Vishal's sarcasm wisely?
qa.a: She stayed generous, acknowledged his strength as a tester, gave him meaningful work, and let time settle things instead of demanding warmth.

qa.q: How might Vishal see Ritu's promotion?
qa.a: Vishal likely feels passed over and envious, since he had applied for the same job.

grounding: The story shows a new manager whose former peer who wanted the job is sarcastic, who stays generous, acknowledges his strengths and gives him meaningful work.

passage:
On her first Monday as sales manager at the Andheri office, Damini brought a box of pedas. Deepak, who had applied for the same job, took one and said, "Sweet. Like the promotion." Everyone looked at their screens.

It continued for a week. Deepak answered her emails with "Noted." He sat at the back in meetings. Damini went home each night feeling hurt and oddly guilty, as if she had stolen something.

She didn't ask him to be friendly. She did something else. In the Thursday meeting she said, "Deepak closed the Ghatkopar distributor last quarter when none of us could. I want him to lead the new western suburbs accounts."

Deepak looked up sharply. There was a pause. "Okay," he said.

It took a month. He was still dry with her. But one Friday he stopped at her desk and said, "The Borivali client wants a meeting. You should come, they like managers." It wasn't warmth yet. It was a start.

qa.q: What did Deepak say when he took a peda?
How did Damini feel going home each night that first week?
qa.a: Damini felt hurt and oddly guilty, as if she had stolen something.

qa.q: What did Damini do instead of demanding friendliness?
qa.a: She publicly acknowledged Deepak's strength and gave him important accounts to lead, then gave the relationship time.

qa.q: How does Deepak seem to experience working under Damini?
qa.a: Deepak seems envious and stung at first, but slowly softens once his skills are recognised.

grounding: The passage shows a new manager whose former peer who wanted the promotion is cool and sarcastic, who stays generous, acknowledges his strengths and lets time settle it.
